Carr played [[college football]] for the [[Fresno State Bulldogs football|Fresno State Bulldogs]], winning the [[Johnny Unitas Golden Arm Award]] and [[Sammy Baugh Trophy]] in 2001. He was selected [[List of first overall National Football League draft picks|first overall]] by the [[Houston Texans]] in the [[2002 NFL draft]] and was the franchise's first draft selection. Carr spent his first five seasons as the Texans' starter, but struggled with inconsistent play. As a rookie, he also set the NFL season record for sacks taken. After being released by Houston, Carr spent the remainder of his career as a backup for the [[Carolina Panthers]], [[New York Giants]], and [[San Francisco 49ers]], winning [[Super Bowl XLVI]] with the Giants. Carr later served as the offensive coordinator at [[Bakersfield Christian High School]] and was an analyst for [[NFL Network]].{{cite web |title=NFL Network cast, hosts and analysts |url=https://www.nfl.com/network/on-air-talent/david-carr-talent |website=NFL.com}}

Selected by the [[Arizona Cardinals]] with the eighth overall pick in the [[1999 NFL draft]], Boston became a [[Pro Bowl]] selection with the Cardinals in 2001. He also played for the [[San Diego Chargers]], [[Miami Dolphins]], and [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]].

'''Dave Yovanovits''' (born March 6, 1981) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was an [[offensive lineman]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Temple Owls football|Temple Owls]], playing in every snap of 40 of 45 games.  He was selected in the [[2003 NFL draft]] by the [[New York Jets]], whom he played for in 2003 and 2004.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2003 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2003/draft.htm |access-date=2023-03-27 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He was released by the Jets in order to reduce salary cap space when the team signed [[Ty Law]] in 2005. Yovanovits made his first career start in the Browns' 20–16 win over the [[Baltimore Ravens]] in their 2005 season finale.<ref>Doerschuk, Steve. [http://www.cantonrep.com/index.php?Category=17&ID=302911&r=4 Rookie Harrison impresses with runs, TD catch] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070927192633/http://www.cantonrep.com/index.php?Category=17&ID=302911&r=4 |date=2007-09-27 }}, cantonrep.com, accessed February 24, 2007.</ref> After briefly joining the [[Detroit Lions]] in December 2006, Yovanovits signed with the [[New Orleans Saints]] on February 16, 2007.<ref>[http://www2.sportsnet.ca/football/nfl/players/Dave_Yovanovits/ Dave Yovanovits] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090106223520/http://www.sportsnet.ca/football/nfl/players/Dave_Yovanovits/ |date=2009-01-06 }}, [[sportsnet.ca]], accessed May 7, 2007.</ref>

Yovanovits played [[high school football]] for [[Hopatcong High School]] in [[Hopatcong, New Jersey]].<ref>{{usurped|1=[https://web.archive.org/web/20070930093647/http://www.databasefootball.com/players/playerpage.htm?ilkid=YOVANDAV01 Dave Yovanovits]}}, database Football, accessed April 12, 2008.</ref> He has been a resident of [[Stanhope, New Jersey]].<ref>Tatum, Kevin. {{usurped|1=[https://web.archive.org/web/20150922052018/http://articles.philly.com/2003-04-28/sports/25474847_1_dan-klecko-temple-coach-bobby-wallace-joe-klecko "Owls pleasantly surprised by draft The Patriots chose defensive lineman Dan Klecko, and the Jets took offensive tackle Dave Yovanovits."]}}, ''[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]]'', April 28, 2013. Accessed October 9, 2015. "At home in Stanhope, N.J., Dave Yovanovits was glued to the televised NFL draft coverage from New York."</ref>

'''David Rodney Croudip''' (January 25, 1958 – October 10, 1988) was an American professional [[American football|football]] [[defensive back]]. '''David Edward Beverly''' (born August 19, 1950) is an American former professional  [[American football|foobball]] player who was a [[Punter (football position)|punter]] for seven seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for the [[Houston Oilers]] and the [[Green Bay Packers]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Auburn Tigers football|Auburn Tigers]].

Beverly played as quarterback and punter for [[Sweet Water High School]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.al.com/erry-2018/02/9893dbd04b/auburns_top_10_nfl_passers_cam.html |title=Auburn's top 10 NFL passers: Cam Newton pads lead |date= February 12, 2018 |author=Inabinett, Mark |work=Al.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.al.com/sports/2016/12/the_no_1_football_player_from.html |title=The No. 1 football player from each of Alabama's 67 counties |date=December 22, 2016 |author=Bennett, Julie |work=[[Al.com]]}}</ref> At the final game of his junior season, he sustained what was thought to be a career-ending knee injury and was unable to play in his senior season.

He enrolled at [[Auburn University]], where he decided to join the football team as a walk-on. While at Auburn, he earned three letters and was named to the 1971 All-Southeastern Conference Team. His net punt yardage averages are still records at Auburn.

After earning his degree, he played for one year for the Houston Oilers in 1974, then went to the Green Bay Packers (1975–80), where he was the starting punter for his tenure there. He still holds the all-time Packer records for career punts (495) and single-season punts (106), with three games in which he punted 10 times, second on the Green Bay list.<ref>{{Cite web | url = https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BeveDa20.htm | website = Pro-Football-Reference.com | access-date = February 29, 2024 | title = David Beverly Stats}}</ref>

Beverly was selected to the Auburn "Team of the Seventies", and was named the best SEC punter of the last 25 years by sports writer Alf Van Hoose. He was also honored in 1973 with a ''David Beverly Day'' in [[Sweet Water, Alabama|Sweet Water]].

'''David Thayer Chapple''' (born March 30, 1947) is an American [[artist]] and former professional [[American football|football]] player. He played as a [[Punter (American football)|punter]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) between 1969 and 1975.

Born in 1947 in [[Palo Alto, California]],<ref>[http://www.derusfinearts.com/bioDAVIDCHAPPLE.html David Chapple Biography, De Rus Fine Arts] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081118200109/http://www.derusfinearts.com/bioDAVIDCHAPPLE.html |date=2008-11-18 }}, accessed 2010-07-24</ref> Chapple was All American in football at [[University of California, Santa Barbara]].  Selected by the [[San Francisco 49ers]] in [[1969 NFL/AFL draft]], Chapple suffered a back injury and wasn't able to play for two years.<ref>[http://www.independent.com/news/2010/apr/06/hall-fame-painting-punter/ The Painting Punter] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120313124223/http://www.independent.com/news/2010/apr/06/hall-fame-painting-punter/ |date=2012-03-13 }}, Santa Barbara Independent, April 6, 2010.</ref> He then signed with the [[Buffalo Bills]] in 1971, playing only a single game. Moving to the [[Los Angeles Rams]] the following year, Chapple was selected to the [[Pro Bowl]] after netting an average of 44.2 yards for the 1972 season, a statistic not bettered until 2007 by [[Shane Lechler]]. After another season and a half, he moved to the [[New England Patriots]] mid-season 1974, finishing his career with the remaining five games.<ref>{{usurped|1=[https://web.archive.org/web/20100212145957/http://databasefootball.com/players/playerpage.htm?ilkid=ChappDav01 DatabaseFootball.com entry]}}, accessed 2010-07-24</ref>

Chapple developed artistic talents at a young age, winning art contests and awards from grammar school. While earning his degree at the University of California at Santa Barbara, Chapple worked in the Santa Barbara Museum of Natural History as a bird taxidermist, which developed his interest in wildlife painting. He started his professional career as an artist in 1970 while playing professional football in Los Angeles, and turned his attention full-time to these artistic pursuits after retiring from football in 1975.

Primarily a contemporary [[oil painter]] in the influence of the early California  [[Impressionism|impressionist]] landscape painters, Chapple has won numerous stamp contests for conservation groups and various state stamps for California, Kentucky, Utah and Idaho.
